available: The ring-class Artin quotient kills principal ideles and completed order units; it is unramified away from the conductor.
needed: The inert K-prime (ell), prime to fn_I, splits completely in H_(fn_I), and its residue field is F_(ell^2).
derivation: The invertible prime ideal equals the rational principal ideal (ell), hence has trivial class in Pic(O_(fn_I)). Unramifiedness and trivial arithmetic Frobenius give complete splitting. Since ell is inert in K/Q, its base residue degree is two; complete splitting does not turn it into an F_ell residue field. This gives F² Xbar=Xbar. The norm and CM reduction identities in H13 remain separate.
premises: Actual imaginary K and allowed conductor fn_I; ell inert, new and prime to conductor; same class-field Artin convention.
The restriction identity H11 and point norm/reduction identities are separate inputs.
